clue.text: A type of reef of gold in California

indicators.note: the word for gold sits inside the abbreviation for the state, as the clue's 'in' says

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A Californian reef full of gold, the stuff of treasure-hunting tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral reefs are one of the main kinds of reef, built by polyp skeletons in warm seas.

clue.text: Berate players over one wicket

indicators.note: in a down answer the actors' word sits over, above, the rest

parts.note: the players in a play are its cast
I is the Roman numeral one
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: Scolding the team for losing a wicket in the over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicket' and 'over' suggest cricket, but a wicket is also a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to criticise severely, the same as scolding.

clue.text: Christmas card character getting round to a petition ?

definitions.meaning: the red-breasted bird is a favourite figure on festive cards
added after 'round' it makes a round-... petition, signed in a circle so no name heads the list

explanation.surface: A Christmas card figure finally getting round to signing a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: The redbreast bird is a seasonal emblem, and a round-robin is a petition with signatures arranged in a ring.

clue.text: Rally is wild about one hundred of these ballads

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the numerals
wild suggests the letters of 'Rally' run riot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral hundred

explanation.surface: A rally goes wild over a hundred songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns RALLY into LYRAL, and 'about' puts IC (one, hundred) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth and Coleridge's 1798 collection was titled Lyrical Ballads, so the word describes ballads of that kind.

clue.text: Sound story-telling skill is no asset

indicators.note: 'Sound' asks the solver to say the phrase out loud and hear another word in it

parts.note: telling stories is lying, so the skill is a 'lie ability'

explanation.surface: Being a good raconteur is said to be no advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective praising the skill, but it tells you the phrase LIE ABILITY, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounts the opposite of an asset is a debt or obligation owed, so something that is no asset is a burden.

clue.text: Note change in Lily's home in The Gap

indicators.note: one musical note in the word is swapped for another note, as the clue says

parts.note: a water lily grows in a lagoon, laguna in Spanish and Italian

explanation.surface: A singer changes note at Lily's home in the town of Gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note change' swaps G for C, both musical notes, in LAGUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacuna is a missing portion or blank space, as in a manuscript.

clue.text: The donkey is riding the boy, though not without help

indicators.note: in a down answer the rider sits on top, so the first two pieces come above the last

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A donkey carrying a boy, who needs some help.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aided is to have received help, the double negative of 'not without'.

clue.text: A heavy burden in copper transport

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A heavy load carried in a copper vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a demon weighing on a sleeper, hence any oppressive weight.

clue.text: In a moment a sailor returns to his love

indicators.note: returns says the last two words are turned back to front

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home to his sweetheart in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A TAR into RATA.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, from the Italian for beloved.

clue.text: Bound for work. Like an egg ? Sound idea !

indicators.note: 'Sound idea' says a word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: an egg has a yolk, so it is yolked

explanation.surface: A worker off to the office, and an egg-shaped idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound idea' looks like praise but signals that YOLKED, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen joined by a wooden collar for ploughing are yoked, bound together for labour.

clue.text: After an erratic burst, turns and takes off

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the jumbled first one, in clue order
something erratic wanders unpredictably, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: turns on a variety bill are acts

explanation.surface: A performer, after an erratic outburst, leaves the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' rearranges BURST into SUBTR, and ACTS follows it as 'After' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To take one number off another is to deduct it, the arithmetic operation of minus.

clue.text: Like the regiment least likely to

definitions.text: Like the regiment least likely to

parts.words: Like the regiment least likely to
parts.note: an elite regiment is described by one word, and the same word is what such a regiment, being the toughest, is least likely to do under pressure

explanation.surface: A description of the most dependable regiment in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The word describes a top regiment, and a crack unit is the one least likely to break, the verb sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-rate, elite unit is called this, and to break down under strain is to give way in the same word's verb sense.

clue.text: Literary Americans doing no harm in Europe

parts.note: harmless people are guiltless ones
to an American, being in Europe means being overseas

explanation.surface: American writers behaving harmlessly on a European tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain's 1869 travel book follows a party of American tourists through Europe and the Holy Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's book title names its American travellers, so they are literary figures from a famous work.

clue.text: Land providing a painter with French corn?.

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter
blé is the French word for wheat or corn

explanation.surface: A field that gives a painter some French corn to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughable farmland is called this, used as a noun for cultivated ground.

clue.text: Vegetable Dowson loved ?

parts.note: the poet Ernest Dowson wrote of his faithfulness to Cynara, and cynara is the botanical genus of a globe vegetable

explanation.surface: Which vegetable did the poet Dowson love?
explanation.walkthrough: Dowson's poem refrain is 'I have been faithful to thee, Cynara!'; Cynara scolymus is the globe artichoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle-like vegetable belongs to the genus Cynara, the name of Dowson's beloved.

clue.text: Home in a conveyance ?

parts.note: a conveyance is not a vehicle but the legal deed transferring property, and the dwelling it describes has an old legal name

explanation.surface: Someone living in a caravan or carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveyance' suggests a vehicle you live in, but it is a property deed, where a house with its land has an old legal name.
explanation.definitionFit: In English property law a dwelling house with its outbuildings and land bears this archaic legal name in deeds.

clue.text: It is necessary to burst into that silent sea

indicators.note: letters that burst apart and reform are rearranged, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Coleridge's Mariner must burst into that silent sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes Coleridge's Ancient Mariner: 'We were the first that ever burst into that silent sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable is required, so the word means needed.

clue.text: Persian Emperor ? Yes, wandering in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes in the county abbreviation

parts.note: Cambs is the standard abbreviation for Cambridgeshire, an English county

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Persian ruler said yes to wandering in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns YES into YSE, which goes inside CAMBS; Cambridgeshire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambyses II, son of Cyrus the Great, was a king of Achaemenid Persia who conquered Egypt.

clue.text: Everlasting kiss inside or outside

indicators.note: the kiss letter goes inside the word for everlasting, as the clue says

parts.note: everlasting means eternal
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An eternal kiss, whether indoors or out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the outer side is exterior, the opposite of internal.

clue.text: Free to find another tenant

definitions.meaning: to free is to let go
to let property again on a new rental agreement

explanation.surface: A free flat while the landlord looks for another tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate something is to let it go, and to re-let property is to lease it once more.

clue.text: Fishy platter-cleaners

parts.note: the nursery rhyme couple who 'licked the platter clean' share their surname with small fish

explanation.surface: Fish that clean up the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean, and between them they licked the platter clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's Jack and his wife are the family who cleaned the platter, and the plural also names small herring-like fish.

clue.text: Medium that confounds a spy with elegance

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: chic means elegance or style

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant baffles a spy with stylishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounds' turns SPY into PSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium claims to contact spirits, a clairvoyant with supposed paranormal powers.

clue.text: Decree Gray's picturesque reformation

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Oscar Wilde's novel is The Picture of Dorian Gray, so the Gray of the picture is Dorian

explanation.surface: An edict from the poet Gray on picturesque reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gray' suggests the poet Thomas Gray, but it is Wilde's Dorian Gray of the portrait; 'reformation' rearranges DORIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order officially, to decree by authority.

clue.text: Fruit, N. European type, growing up in Missouri

parts.note: a huckleberry is a dark North American berry
a Finn is a native of Finland in northern Europe

explanation.surface: A northern European fruit variety cultivated in Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain's boy hero grows up on the Mississippi in Missouri.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain's ragged boy hero is a character raised in a Missouri river town, the 'type' growing up there.

clue.text: Pets — of the Big Bad Wolf ?

definitions.meaning: in the fairy tale the wolf threatens to blow the house down with puffs and blows

explanation.surface: Asking which pets belong to the Big Bad Wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pet' is also a sulk; the wolf in The Three Little Pigs 'huffed and puffed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulks and fits of pique are both pets and huffs, and the fairy-tale wolf blows hard in huffs and puffs.

clue.text: Fibre for repairing stile

indicators.note: repairing remakes something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fibre used for mending a stile.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre from Mexican agave, used for cords and brushes.

clue.text: A negative if backward girl

indicators.note: backward says the whole run of words is read from the end

parts.note: no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: An unenthusiastic, slow-witted girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns A NO IF round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's name, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: Past eight ? Change for dinner

indicators.note: 'Change' tells you to rearrange the letters of the phrase before it

explanation.surface: It's gone eight o'clock, time to dress for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change for dinner' reads as dressing up, but 'Change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long pasta strands make a common evening meal.

clue.text: A good man has level money on the writer

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword's good man
evens, or even money, is a bet at level odds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A virtuous man bets at even money on an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island; evens is a betting term for odds of one to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, author of Kidnapped and Treasure Island.

clue.text: Many 'wind up in a basket

parts.note: C, the Roman hundred, stands for many
to reel in a line is to wind it up

explanation.surface: Many people end up in a basket case.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker container for the catch has this name.
